governanceNotes: Authored conservatively at ASSOCIATION_ONLY strength with reverse causality recorded: endometriosis is itself identified as the leading cause of chronic pelvic pain (Sieberg 2020), so the direction of the association is contested; the comorbidity is documented in mechanism reviews and cohort-adjacent clinical series, but CPP populations are heavily confounded by comorbid interstitial cystitis/bladder pain syndrome, IBS, pelvic-floor dysfunction, and central sensitization, so no directional claim is supportable at the mapping level.

Mechanism-category boundary recorded: sensitization mechanisms in CPP are documented across the literature (Yong 2022 hyperalgesic priming; Yong 2017 central sensitization underlying genito-pelvic pain penetration disorder); the edge is categorized PSYCHOPHYSIOLOGICAL to reflect the sensitization-mediated comorbidity without asserting endometriosis tissue as the direct nociceptor source.

nexusClaim.associationBasis: The narrative review of endometriosis-related pain identifies endometriosis as the leading cause of chronic pelvic pain, with mechanisms contributing to CPP reviewed across central and peripheral sensitization (Sieberg 2020); the deep-dyspareunia framework documents that half of women with endometriosis experience deep dyspareunia and that CPP in endometriosis is multifactorial, with comorbid interstitial cystitis/bladder pain syndrome and central sensitization as active contributors (Yong 2017); the deep-dyspareunia quality-of-life review documents recurrent dysmenorrhea causing hyperalgesic priming that sensitizes the nervous system, leading to chronic pelvic pain (Yong 2022).
nexusClaim.causationStatus: Neither causation nor aggravation is established at the mapping level, and the direction is contested: endometriosis is itself the leading cause of CPP, so CPP as a source condition may reflect undiagnosed endometriosis rather than causing it, CPP populations carry heavy confounding from comorbid bladder-pain syndrome, IBS, pelvic-floor dysfunction, and central sensitization, and the cited evidence is review class without longitudinal onset-ordering data, so no directional claim is made here.

causalMechanism.primaryVector: A sensitization-mediated pathway is hypothesized: chronic pelvic pain maintains repeated nociceptive input from the pelvis, driving central sensitization and hyperalgesic priming that lower pain thresholds across pelvic viscera and amplify inflammatory signaling; within this sensitized state, cyclic hormonal and inflammatory fluctuations are hypothesized to facilitate the survival, adherence, and progression of ectopic endometrial implants, while sensitization also amplifies the pain those implants produce, making the association bidirectional in presentation. The mechanism is plausible and discussed in the literature, but the directionality remains unproven and the evidence base is review class, so no directional claim is made here.

evidentiaryProfile.conservativeRationale: This relationship is supported as an association only. Endometriosis and chronic pelvic pain co-occur at high rates and share sensitization mechanisms, but the direction is contested and confounding is pervasive; individual determination requires laparoscopic or imaging documentation of endometriosis with chronology relative to the pain syndrome, exclusion of comorbid pain generators, and review by a qualified medical professional.
evidentiaryProfile.evidenceGaps: Laparoscopic or imaging documentation of endometriosis (stage, location, histology where obtained) with chronology relative to chronic pelvic pain onset; pain characterization records (cyclic versus non-cyclic, dyspareunia, dysmenorrhea) from a qualified clinician; workup excluding comorbid interstitial cystitis/bladder pain syndrome, irritable bowel syndrome, pelvic-floor dysfunction, and myofascial pain as alternative pain sources; surgical or treatment-response records correlating implant burden with pain course; a medical professional's opinion connecting the documented findings in this individual case
alternativeEtiologiesToRuleOut: Undiagnosed endometriosis as the primary CPP driver (reverse causality)
Interstitial cystitis or bladder pain syndrome
Irritable bowel syndrome and functional GI pain
Central sensitization syndromes independent of pelvic pathology

suggestions.rationale: Authored conservatively at association-only strength: the comorbidity is well documented but the direction is contested (endometriosis is a leading cause of CPP), the evidence is review class without longitudinal onset ordering, and comorbid pain generators confound attribution; the edge records co-occurrence only and leaves every causal judgment to a qualified medical professional.
